g.text: As large language models become capable of autonomous economic action, a new
paradigm of agentic commerce is emerging where AI agents search, negotiate,
and transact on behalf of human principals (Rothschild et al., 2025).
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=1) As large language models become capable of autonomous economic action, a new paradigm of agentic commerce is emerging where AI agents search, negotiate, and transact on behalf of human principals (Rothschild et al., 2025).

g.text: This shift promises efficiency gains through automated discovery and
negotiation, but introduces fundamental challenges in marketplace design.
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=0) This shift promises efficiency gains through automated discovery and negotiation, but introduces fundamental challenges in marketplace design.

g.text: Info bottleneck at large consideration sets
When agents must evaluate large consideration sets—hundreds of potential
sellers matching a customer's query—they face an information bottleneck that
human-designed interfaces were never built to address.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) When agents must evaluate large consideration sets—hundreds of potential sellers matching a customer's query—they face an information bottleneck that human-designed interfaces were never built to address.

g.text: The core problem is that marketplace search results typically present
truncated natural language descriptions that lose critical fit signals.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) The core problem is that marketplace search results typically present truncated natural language descriptions that lose critical fit signals.

g.text: A customer seeking specific menu items, amenities, and budget constraints
cannot reliably determine from a 40-token description snippet whether a
restaurant carries the requested dishes or falls within budget.
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=0) A customer seeking specific menu items, amenities, and budget constraints cannot reliably determine from a 40-token description snippet whether a restaurant carries the requested dishes or falls within budget.

g.text: At scale, this information loss compounds: agents contact businesses based
on incomplete signals, accumulate irrelevant context from poor-fit
interactions, and exhibit first-proposal bias that locks in suboptimal early
g.title: N6 [Context] (cites=1) At scale, this information loss compounds: agents contact businesses based on incomplete signals, accumulate irrelevant context from poor-fit interactions, and exhibit first-proposal bias that locks in suboptimal early matches (Bansal et al., 2025).

g.text: In our experiments with 100 businesses, the baseline
waste over 90% of their interactions on businesses that
g.title: N7 [Result] (cites=0) In our experiments with 100 businesses, the baseline system achieves only 7.8% contacted-fit rate—agents waste over 90% of their interactions on businesses that cannot satisfy customer requirements.

g.text: A natural hypothesis is that agent-side interventions—better prompting or
more inference compute—can overcome this information bottleneck.
g.title: N8 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) A natural hypothesis is that agent-side interventions—better prompting or more inference compute—can overcome this information bottleneck.
N9 [Limitation] (cites=0) Our experiments reject this hypothesis.

g.text: Prompting agents to explicitly extract fit signals from
truncated descriptions actually hurts welfare, dropping
it from 68.51 to −35.85: agents become more selective
but without sufficient information to act on, leading…
g.title: N10 [Result] (cites=0) Prompting agents to explicitly extract fit signals from truncated descriptions actually hurts welfare, dropping it from 68.51 to −35.85: agents become more selective but without sufficient information to act on, leading to misdirected selectivity.

g.text: Inference scaling fares no better: providing 4.7× more
LLM calls and forcing agents to explore multiple
additional computation cannot recover information lost…
g.title: N11 [Result] (cites=0) Inference scaling fares no better: providing 4.7× more LLM calls and forcing agents to explore multiple options yields negative welfare (−29.71) because additional computation cannot recover information lost during description truncation.

g.text: These failures reveal that the bottleneck is information, not reasoning
g.title: N12 [Limitation] (cites=0) These failures reveal that the bottleneck is information, not reasoning capacity.

g.text: We propose Fit Cards, a platform-side intervention that replaces truncated
g.title: N13 [Method] (cites=0) We propose Fit Cards, a platform-side intervention that replaces truncated descriptions with query-conditioned structured metadata.

g.text: Rather than presenting generic text snippets, the platform computes fit
signals—how many requested items are available, which amenities match, and
the estimated price—directly from its structured catalog.
g.title: N14 [Method] (cites=0) Rather than presenting generic text snippets, the platform computes fit signals—how many requested items are available, which amenities match, and the estimated price—directly from its structured catalog.

g.text: Results are sorted by relevance with explicit rank labels, enabling agents
to identify high-fit businesses at a glance.
g.title: N15 [Method] (cites=0) Results are sorted by relevance with explicit rank labels, enabling agents to identify high-fit businesses at a glance.

g.text: In experiments on a restaurant marketplace with 100
businesses, Fit Cards achieve 11.4× higher welfare than
the status quo baseline while using 28% fewer LLM
g.title: N16 [Result] (cites=0) In experiments on a restaurant marketplace with 100 businesses, Fit Cards achieve 11.4× higher welfare than the status quo baseline while using 28% fewer LLM calls.

interventions fail because truncated descriptions lose
fit signals that agents cannot recover through…
g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We identify the information bottleneck in agentic marketplace search, showing that agent-side interventions fail because truncated descriptions lose fit signals that agents cannot recover through reasoning.

g.text: We propose Fit Cards, a platform-side intervention that
g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose Fit Cards, a platform-side intervention that surfaces query-conditioned structured metadata computed from the platform's catalog.

g.text: We demonstrate that Fit Cards improve contacted-fit
rate from 7.8% to 73.6%, validating that better
g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) We demonstrate that Fit Cards improve contacted-fit rate from 7.8% to 73.6%, validating that better discovery-stage contact selection drives welfare improvements.

g.text: We show that discovery-stage interventions are more
first-proposal bias persists but does not dominate
welfare when agents contact high-fit businesses.
g.title: C4 [Contribution] (cites=0) We show that discovery-stage interventions are more effective than proposal-stage interventions: first-proposal bias persists but does not dominate welfare when agents contact high-fit businesses.
